```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Query a Warehouse, Lakehouse SQL endpoint, or Fabric SQL Database using the
visitor's Microsoft account. The same sign-in can also support workspace
discovery, OneLake, and semantic model queries through fabricQueryR.

## Start with SQL

Install `fabricQueryR` and `odbc`, plus Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL
Server. Copy the server and database from the item's SQL connection settings.
Users need access to the item and data; see
[Fabric SQL connectivity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/data-warehouse/connectivity).

Create an Entra Web app registration with delegated SQL access and register
`http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI. Start with `services = "sql"`;
you can add the permissions for other Fabric services as your app needs them.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "sql",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_fabric_sql(
    auth$connection,
    server = "example.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com",
    database = "Reporting"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER AS database_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

The query shows the database identity. Replace it with SQL for your tables,
or use dbplyr with the connection returned by `con()`.

## Discover workspaces

To add workspace discovery, change the client's services to
`services = c("sql", "fabric")` and configure the registration's delegated
Fabric workspace-read permission. Add `verbatimTextOutput("workspaces")`
to the UI, then put this inside `server()`:

```{r workspaces}
fabric <- oauth_db_fabric_api(auth$connection)

output$workspaces <- renderPrint({
  fabric$call(fabricQueryR::fabric_workspaces)
})
```

`$call()` takes a fabricQueryR function and its usual arguments. It supplies
the visitor's credentials and returns the function's normal result.

## Choose additional services

Add the services your app uses to `oauth_db_microsoft_client()`. Each also
needs the corresponding delegated permissions in the Entra registration:

| `services` entry | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `"sql"` | Warehouse, Lakehouse SQL endpoint, and SQL Database |
| `"fabric"` | Workspace and item discovery |
| `"onelake"` | OneLake files and tables |
| `"dax"` | Semantic model queries |
| `"kql"` | KQL queries |
| `"graphql"` | GraphQL queries |

The preset requests tokens for those services; users still need access to
the relevant workspace, items, and data. SQL access alone doesn't grant
OneLake or semantic model access.

For KQL, include `"kql"` in the client's services. With `fabric` created as
above, replace the table output with:

```{r kql}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  fabric$call(
    fabricQueryR::fabric_kql_query,
    cluster = "https://example.kusto.fabric.microsoft.com",
    database = "Events",
    query = "Events | take 20"
  )
})
```

## Work with Lakehouse and semantic model objects

fabricQueryR's resource objects offer methods for reading data. Configure
`services = c("fabric", "onelake")` for the following example, or add those
services to the SQL app's client. Put discovery in a reactive expression so
a change of account obtains a new object:

```{r lakehouse}
lakehouse <- reactive({
  fabric$call(
    fabricQueryR::fabric_item,
    workspace = "workspace-guid",
    item = "lakehouse-guid"
  )
})

output$rows <- renderTable({
  lakehouse()$read_table("Orders", limit = 100L)
})
```

These are fabricQueryR's own R6 objects. A Warehouse offers
`$sql_query(sql)`; a semantic model offers `$dax_query(dax)`. Include
`"sql"` or `"dax"` respectively in the client's services. See
fabricQueryR's help for the other methods and their arguments.

## Connection options and custom sign-in

The SQL helper uses fabricQueryR's ODBC backend by default. To use ADBC,
install fabricQueryR's ADBC dependencies and the MSSQL driver, then pass
`backend = "adbc"` to `oauth_db_fabric_sql()`. Other options, such as
`timeout` and `read_only`, go to `fabricQueryR::fabric_sql_connect()`.

Use the SQL helper for a DBI connection managed by shinyOAuthDB. Connections
opened by native API functions or resource methods belong to your app.
For a direct native function call, `token = fabric$token_provider()` supplies
the callback; `?oauth_db_fabric` shows the single-service alternative.

If an existing shinyOAuth client uses different target names, supply the
service-to-target mapping when creating the API client:

```{r targets}
fabric <- oauth_db_fabric_api(
  auth$connection,
  targets = c(fabric = "discovery", sql = "reporting", onelake = "files")
)
```

This mapping replaces the defaults and lists the services available to the
client. Use `targets = list(kql = NULL)` for one service without named
targets. DAX and GraphQL share the Power BI resource and must use the same
target; different resources need different targets.

See [Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) for permission checks,
multiple accounts, and cached results.
